title: Tamar and the Missing Whistle
markdown:
Morning burst like a bright buttery biscuit. Sunbeams poked Tamar the sheepdog’s nose. A cool breeze shot through the barn, grass and clover riding it. He stretched from twitching ears to thumping tail. Today felt like a starting gun.

He bounded out to greet the flock — and stopped. His bright blue whistle, the loud one, the keep-together one, was gone. Paws wobbled. Tail drooped. Without it the sheep would scatter like marbles.

A shadow zipped. Kiki the kestrel, button-black eyes. “Trouble, Tamar?”

“My whistle. Vanished.”

“Bright blue? I’ll watch from up top.” She punched into the sky.

Tamar’s paws itched. He dashed past the sleepy sheep, nose to the ground, sniff sniff sniff. The old apple tree? Nope. The sunny stone wall? Not there. He peeked under Farmer Giles’s rusty spade. Dust and a disappointed beetle. Absolutely nothing.

“Anything, Kiki? Anything?”

“Just a rabbit munching near the carrots. Keep looking. Don’t quit.”

He scrambled up the winding dusty sheep track. Steep. The wind howled like a grumpy giant and pushed him back. A faint tweet-tweet teased him. He barked, hopeful. “Whistle? Is that you?” The sound got lost in the breeze.

Kiki swooped lower, gliding near green ferns. “That’s the wind playing tricks, pushing sound downhill. Call into it. Let it carry you uphill.”

He planted his paws, faced the rush, and bellowed. The gust grabbed the word WHISTLE and posted it toward the peaks.

A clear tweet came back from the whispering pines.

“That way,” Kiki cried, already an arrow.

Tamar bounded forward, paws flying over rocks, dodging thorny bushes. This climb felt different. He was not only chasing a lost whistle. He was chasing a sound that proved he still had a voice without brass. Kiki shot ahead, a darting arrow, scanning every twig. “There. Tangled in the thick brambles by the tallest pine.”

His heart thumped. He raced. And there it was: bright blue, caught on a sharp thorn, glinting. He nudged it free with his nose. Success. A happy bark. Kiki swooped, cheering.

The whistle was smooth and familiar in his mouth. He had found it with a brave run, stubborn paws, and a kestrel who listened to weather. Tail became a blur.

“We did it.”

“You didn’t quit.”

“You heard the wind.”

He tucked the whistle safe — and knew, bright as the biscuit morning, that he was still Tamar with or without it. The flock lifted their heads. He tore back down the track, Kiki slicing the blue above him, ready for the whole loud day.

Today was already running. Tamar ran with it.
